Here's your space and defense news for Monday, Nov 2, covering Friday through this morning.

Top stories: The US approved a $2.1B sale of 500 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine, paid for by allies, though deliveries may not arrive until after 2030. Drones entered Romania again on Oct 31, and sea-drone strikes on Black Sea shipping are continuing. Google is reportedly in early talks to help secure the data behind Golden Dome.

NATO

  • NATO's Allied Command Transformation finished nearly two weeks of experiments in Latvia. They tested 5G-based passive detection, layered counter-drone defense and AI-assisted targeting, with more than 30 nations, 100 companies and nearly 400 drones taking part. The chair of NATO's Military Committee wants a shared system that links sensors to weapons across nations against drone swarms, fielded on the eastern flank next year. NATO ACT
  • On Oct 31, two drones entered northeastern Romania and F-16s were scrambled. One drone was last seen inside the country. Earlier in the week, Romania, Bulgaria and Türkiye agreed to coordinate on Black Sea security, and a ninth merchant ship was hit off Bulgaria. Vigil Consilium weekly brief
  • On Oct 30, Bulgaria signed on to NATO's joint effort against threats flying below 150 m, such as drones, cruise missiles and glide bombs. Bulgaria's parliament still has to ratify it. Bytes Europe

European Union

  • The Commission's second call for the €21.3B left in SAFE defense loans is drawing new interest. Ireland is reconsidering a bid after its finance ministry vetoed one last year. Irish Times
  • After sea drones sank the container ship Contship Jet, a European Parliament defense delegation visited Bulgaria. MEPs said states on the EU's eastern border could get up to 10% more in the 2028–34 EU budget, and Bulgaria is asking for an extra €2B. The article is in Bulgarian. Capital.bg
  • Germany's defense procurement office ordered two new Patriot fire units to replace the ones it gave Ukraine in 2025, plus repair kits packed in containers. The article is in German. Presseportal / BAAINBw
  • MBDA Deutschland won a German armed forces contract to build a demonstrator for an aircraft-mounted laser, an early step toward using lasers from aircraft against drones and cruise missiles. The article is in German. hartpunkt

United States

  • The State Department approved a possible sale of 500 PAC-3 MSE missiles to Ukraine for about $2.1B. Canada, Germany, Norway and EU-backed funds will pay for all of it. This is only an early-stage notice and won't fix Kyiv's near-term shortage. Breaking Defense
  • The Army gave Lockheed Martin a deal worth about $1.08B to develop and test the PAC-3 Edge for its Future Interceptor program. The Army is putting in $660M and Lockheed $423M. Testing starts next year, with full rollout targeted for 2031. Stars and Stripes
  • Bloomberg reports that Google is in early talks to join a Pentagon industry group that would secure the data feeding Golden Dome's command-and-control software. Aalyria is involved, and nothing has been decided. The Next Web
  • SDA Director GP Sandhoo says the first missile-tracking satellites have slipped to next spring. 84 Tranche 1 transport satellites are in orbit now, out of about 474 planned through Tranche 3. SatNews
  • The Space Force program for buying extra commercial space capacity in an emergency has signed its first purchase agreements, with six companies that track objects in orbit. Space Intel Report
  • The Space Force's new multinational war game, Partner to Win, runs this week in Florida with South Korea, the Netherlands, Sweden, Poland and Brazil. It's South Korea's first time taking part. Yonhap
  • Tomorrow's midterms could change the push for more military space and missile defense spending. Most of the $17.5B FY27 Golden Dome request is in the $350B budget reconciliation package, which is still uncertain. SpaceNews
  • The FY27 defense authorization bill (the NDAA) is still in informal talks among congressional staff. The leaders of the House and Senate Armed Services committees will take it up after the election and aim to finish by Thanksgiving. Fights over its total budget and limits on the Iran war could break the bill's 65-year streak of passing. NDAA news roundup
  • The Pentagon said its FY26 Military Intelligence Program budget is $30.9B, about $3B more than FY25. US fighters are also back on air-defense alert at Eareckson Air Station in the Aleutians. Air & Space Forces Magazine
  • Oshkosh Defense is teaming with Grid Aero to mass-produce the Lifter, an autonomous drone for cargo and surveillance. They aim to build hundreds to thousands of them by the early 2030s. Breaking Defense
  • SpaceX flew its 700th Falcon 9 on Oct 30, launching 27 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg, as it winds down Falcon in favor of Starship. Starship's 15th flight, which will try to catch the upper stage, is expected in mid-November. Spaceflight Now

European space

  • ESA chief Josef Aschbacher is in the UAE this week looking for partners beyond the US. The talks include a possible lunar rover launch and an Emirati astronaut flying on ESA's planned crewed mission to the ISS. Reuters via Investing.com
  • Greece's ERMIS-3 CubeSat made the first laser link between a LEO satellite and Greece. It was built with ESA support and carries an Astrolight laser terminal. It now runs two links a day and has room for up to 10 Gbps. ESA
  • Eutelsat's first-quarter LEO revenue rose 30% to €70.9M thanks to OneWeb growth, while video revenue fell nearly 18%. Its order backlog is €12.1B, including €8.9B for IRIS². SatNews

Global space & defense

  • Russia launched 433 drones at Ukraine overnight into Nov 1, hitting 16 locations. RBC-Ukraine
  • It followed up with 326 more drones and six Banderol cruise missiles during the day. Ukrainska Pravda
  • Zelensky wants allies to lend Ukraine 10 to 30 interceptors now, to be paid back from the new US Patriot sale, since those deliveries reportedly won't come until after 2030. Kyiv Post
  • China now has 231 Guowang and 248 Qianfan satellites in orbit for its two LEO broadband networks, which together plan more than 28,000. Orbital Radar
